newsitem.title: UK: Channel Rail Link team deny funding crisis report.
newsitem.headline: Channel Rail Link team deny funding crisis report.

text.p: London and Continental Railways (LCR), the British consortium behind the 3.4 billion pounds ($5.4 billion) Channel Tunnel Rail Link project, denied a report that it is seeking to sell off land in a bid to solve a funding crisis.
A report in The Guardian newspaper on Wednesday said the government may allow LCR to sell land at Kings Cross and Stratford, to raise funds to save the project.
The report said the planned flotation of LCR itself, including its Eurostar passenger rail service, which runs through the Channel Tunnel, also faced delay.
But Jeremy Candfield, LCR director of corporate affairs, told Reuters: "The facts are we are planning a float in early to mid-1998. That has always been the plan and we are on track to do that."

He said there was no funding crisis, claiming almost all the cost of building the rail link to the Channel Tunnel would be funded through LCR's flotation. This is expected to raise more than one billion pounds from an equity issue and a further several billion in debt.
"There is simply no question of us seeking agreement for more land sales to bail out the project," said Candfield.

He he said that LCR had asked permission to sell "small sites" for redevelopment. He denied the amount raised would be material to the funding of the rail link project but refused to comment on how much the sales could raise.
The LCR consortium comprises of Virgin Group, National Express Group Plc, SBC Warburg, engineering group Bechtel and London Electricity Plc, which is owned by U.S. group Entergy.
The rail link will be one of the biggest civil engineering projects in Britain this century and will be partly financed with a 1.4 billion pounds government subsidy.
The link will run for 66 miles between London Waterloo station and the Folkestone coastal connection to the Channel Tunnel which is owned by Eurotunnel Plc. ($ = 0.633 British Pounds)
